recentItems.title: Border Force seizes 1.7m cigarettes, thousands of vapes in WA, NT raids | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
More than a dozen businesses in the Top End have been raided as part of a major illegal tobacco bust, from car yards and clothing stores to grocers and petrol stations.

During a six-day blitz, authorities say they seized more than 300,000 illegal cigarettes and 1,500 vapes in the fourth major operation aimed at disrupting the Territory's black-market trade. 

Courtney Barrett-Peters has this report for ABC News Northern Territory.

recentItems.title: NSW govt unveils major housing proposals for Sydney's east and Parramatta | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The NSW government has earmarked high rise apartment towers up to 34 storeys for Sydney's eastern suburbs, more than ten floors higher than initially planned.
Some locals told the ABC the rezoning will make their suburbs unliveable, but Premier Chris Minns said the city's east needs to "do its bit" to help solve the housing supply crisis.
Parramatta in Western Sydney was also flagged to receive 470 residential dwellings and 500 units as part of its metro precinct project.

recentItems.title: Several bat species detected near Sydney Opera House in conservation program | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Researchers have been delighted to discover three threatened bat species cruising around the Sydney Opera House and surrounds.
The bats were detected as part of a program to better understand their habitats and help them survive.
Ingrid Emery is the executive director of conservation programs at the NSW Department of Environment.
She says the research highlights that green spaces in urban settings are "crucial" to conservation.

recentItems.title: Why insiders say Australian gas got so expensive | The Business | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Australia's gas industry, a national titan that's one of the country's biggest exporters, has been in the headlines for years but for the wrong reasons. Now, with a federal gas reservation scheme on the horizon, the industry's united front is splintering, revealing deep frustrations with one player - Santos.  Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Financial says the tensions stem from the once-in-a-generation investment boom that opened up the country's east coast gas market to exports.  GLNG, or Gladstone LNG, is one of three giant gas export plants built on Curtis Island in Queensland last decade.  It is operated by Santos and counts South Korea's KOGAS and Malaysia's PETRONAS among its investors. Saul Kavonic says Santos was alone in building its plant without having the gas to fill it and needed to buy gas out of the domestic market just to meet its contracts.  Grattan Institute analysis of ACCC data shows GLNG is the only Queensland exporter to have consistently taken more gas from the domestic market than it provides. It's all a far cry from the way Santos pitched the project to governments and the public.  At the time, Santos stressed GLNG would have "no direct implications for domestic gas prices" and that it would "not divert gas from local markets to export markets".  The company told regulators the development was "therefore unlikely to contribute to a future shortage of gas in the domestic market".  But even as Santos was assuring the public on one hand, it was telling shareholders a very different story.  Investor presentations from 2011 show Santos knew opening Australia's eastern market to exports would lead to "permanent … upward pressure on gas prices".  As one of Australia's biggest oil and gas operators, it said this exposure would transform Santos' fortunes and be a commercial boon.

Former company insiders say Santos always knew it lacked the gas reserves to fully supply the current plant. While one former minister acknowledges GLNG should never have been approved without domestic supply obligations. Federal Resources Minister Madeleine King said the best time to have introduced a domestic reservation policy on the east coast was before that export industry commenced.  But she declined to be drawn on the historic decisions made by Santos and GLNG.  She says the government is not interested in pointing the "finger of blame" at any one player and that "gas exploration is complex".

The former boss of Woodside, Peter Coleman ruffled feathers in 2017 when he warned the industry would risk its social licence if it allowed shortages to emerge and prices to rocket. He said "what we've seen over the last 10 years is now those words play out ...The companies have a license or a right to develop it, but at the end of the day, the resource itself is owned by the people and we have an obligation to ensure that endowment is used in the best way possible." 

Paul Farrow, the national secretary of the Australian Workers Union, says the company knew all along it did not have sufficient gas resources to cover its export commitments.  He says the consequences of that decision have been disastrous for gas users such as manufacturers, many of whom employ his members.  

Santos said it had historically contributed the most of any exporter during winter and neither GLNG nor the Queensland LNG industry had caused gas shortages or price spikes.  A spokesperson said GLNG does not intend to contract new gas supply from the domestic market to meet any LNG shortfalls from this year onwards.

With a draft reservation plan due within weeks, the federal government say it's determined to secure the equivalent of 20 per cent of LNG exports for the local market and won't jeopardies exporters' contracts to do it.  Saul Kavonic says Santos will use its formidable lobbying skills to escape – or kill – any reservation policy on the grounds of sovereign risk. recentItems.title: NT Deputy Chief Minister's family link at Beetaloo Digital | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
NT Deputy Chief Minister Gerard Maley has spruiked Beetaloo Digital's plans for a hyperscale data centre to be built near Darwin, despite his sister-in-law working for the firm.

Mr Maley and his sister-in-law, Bethaney Maley, say they have made all the required disclosures to the NT government and Beetaloo Digital.

The Centre for Public Integrity is calling for more transparency in how NT ministerial code of conduct declarations are made. Matt Garrick has this report for ABC News Northern Territory.

recentItems.title: ASX closes at 6-week low as odds of another interest rate rise increase | Finance Report | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The Australian share market ended at its lowest level in six weeks on Tuesday, shedding 1 per cent at the close of trade.

It came after Westpac became the last of the big four banks to change its interest rate forecast, with it now predicting the Reserve Bank of Australia will lift rates to 4.6 per cent at its meeting in November.

recentItems.title: Indonesia's wildfire haze is crossing borders | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Haze from Indonesia’s wildfires has spread across borders, affecting communities in Malaysia and the Philippines.
 
Residents tell the ABC they've experienced darker skies, breathing difficulties, sore throats and a strong smell of smoke, while some Malaysians say the haze has become a frustrating, almost annual occurrence.
 
By Raffa Athallah for ABC News.
